prompt: An object moves in a horizontal plane. In which situation is the object NOT accelerating?
options: An aircraft travels at constant speed along a straight horizontal runway.
A racing car rounds a circular bend at constant speed.
A train slows down along a straight track.
A cyclist accelerates from rest along a straight path.

answer.explanation: Acceleration is zero only when both the magnitude and the direction of velocity remain unchanged. An aircraft moving at constant speed along a straight line has constant velocity, so acceleration is zero.

distractor_explanations: Correct: with constant speed and fixed straight direction, velocity does not change, so a = 0.
A car rounding a bend changes its direction continuously, so velocity changes and acceleration is non-zero.
A train slowing down changes its speed, so velocity changes and acceleration is non-zero.
A cyclist starting from rest increases speed, so velocity changes and acceleration is non-zero.
hints: Acceleration requires a change in velocity.
Can velocity change if speed stays constant? Yes, if direction changes.
solution: A. The aircraft has constant speed and constant direction, so its acceleration is zero.
teacher_walkthrough: Review the three ways velocity can change: speed up, slow down, or change direction.
Only situation 1 maintains both constant speed and constant direction.
Point out that circular motion at constant speed involves continuous acceleration.
